neighbours.label: Plain-language health advice about catching or preventing common illness (vaccine-preventable diseases, colds, staying well); best guess, weak
fire: Babies who miss their shots can catch vaccine-preventable diseases such as measles.
Cover your mouth when you cough, and keep away from others while you are ill.
Nobody should feel ashamed when a toddler picks up a cold at nursery.
Older adults are urged to get vaccine protection before flu season begins.
Drink plenty of water, rest well, and stay in bed when you have a fever.
Chickenpox and rubella are vaccine-preventable illnesses that still spread in schools.
It is not your fault if your child catches the flu from a classmate.
Rinse the cut, keep it clean, and see a nurse if you feel unwell.
quiet: Drivers who miss their turn can take the next exit such as junction nine.
Cover your plants when it snows, and keep away from the pond while it is frozen.
Nobody should feel ashamed when a toddler spills some juice at nursery.
Older adults are urged to get travel tickets before the holiday season begins.
Bring plenty of water, pack well, and stay on the path when you reach the ridge.
Chess and checkers are board games that still spread in schools.
It is not your fault if your child loses a glove on the bus.
Sand the shelf, keep it dry, and see a carpenter if it starts to bend.
